description: We are exploring the history and legacy of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars through creative storytelling and visual media. Looking forward to putting together an impactful project submission!
summary: Vanguard Debris Protocol is an interactive storytelling archive designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon and Mars. By turning mission logs, landing coordinates, and engineering milestones into an accessible digital museum, the project helps young learners explore where historic NASA hardware rests, what scientific discoveries each mission enabled, and why preserving off-world heritage matters for future exploration. Instead of viewing retired landers and rovers as forgotten space debris, students experience them as humanity’s earliest archaeological landmarks across the solar system.
details:
What It Does & How It Works Vanguard Debris Protocol is an interactive web archive and visual storytelling guide created specifically for school-age space enthusiasts. Users can filter between Lunar and Martian exploration sites to inspect six iconic NASA missions whose hardware remains on other worlds: the Apollo 11 Eagle Descent Stage, Surveyor 3 (visited by Apollo 12), the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle, the Opportunity Mars Rover, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and the Viking 1 Lander. Each interactive mission card presents exact landing coordinates, operational timelines, kid-friendly scientific takeaways, and current preservation status.

Benefits & Intended Impact Space science often feels distant or overly technical for younger students. By framing retired spacecraft as "silent sentinels" and off-world archaeological artifacts, our project sparks curiosity about planetary science, robotics, and aerospace engineering while teaching the importance of responsible space exploration and lunar heritage preservation.

Tools, Languages & Development Built using semantic HTML5, modern CSS3 (responsive grid layout and custom space-themed UI), and vanilla JavaScript for instant category filtering, alongside a structured 6-slide visual presentation. All mission coordinates, dates, and scientific achievements were verified against official NASA open portals.

Super Intelligence (SI) Acknowledgment Super Intelligence (LLM) tools were utilized to assist in structuring educational copy, formatting HTML/CSS code, and organizing NASA archival references.
